Consult Summary:
- 53-year-old male with painless swelling and slight warmth over the left elbow for one week, consistent with likely olecranon bursitis; blood tests and anti-inflammatory therapy planned.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Swelling over the left elbow, noticed one week ago.
- No pain reported, only slight warmth and possible fluid sensation on palpation.
- No preceding trauma or injury to the elbow.
- No functional limitation; full range of movement maintained.
- Slight discomfort or "weird" feeling next to the swelling upon palpation.
- No history of similar swelling previously.
- No associated systemic symptoms reported (systems review limited).
- No dry skin elsewhere, no history of eczema.
- Joint sometimes painful due to known osteoarthritis (see PMH).
- Reports that swelling is not worsening and may be improving.

Past Medical History:
- Osteoarthritis: Diagnosed by GP several years ago; occasionally painful joints.
- Allergy: Peanuts.
- No known drug allergies.
- No other significant illnesses reported.
- Medications: None.

Social History:
- Occupation: Desk job, not physically demanding.
- Physical activity: Runs 2–3 times per week.
- No smoking, alcohol, or other substance use mentioned.
- No relevant financial or lifestyle concerns noted.

Family History:
- No known family history of rheumatological diseases (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, lupus).
- No other family history provided.

Physical Examination:
- Visual inspection via video: Swelling over left elbow, slightly warm compared to surrounding skin, skin on tip appears dry.
- Tenderness: No significant tenderness on the tip of elbow; slight discomfort next to the swelling.
- Preserved range of motion.
- No other examination findings documented.
- Vitals not documented.

Investigations:
- Planned: Blood tests including inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatological antibodies, and tests for gout.
- No prior or current investigation results available.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Left elbow swelling, likely bursitis (olecranon bursitis)
  - Plan:
    - Start anti-inflammatory medication: Ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food. Stop if heartburn occurs. (OTC; dose/route/frequency specified.)
    - Blood tests to be arranged for inflammatory markers, infection, autoimmune/rheumatological markers, and uric acid (gout screen).
    - Follow-up after blood test results (clinic or remote review based on patient preference).
    - Advise urgent review if symptoms worsen (increased redness, pain, spreading, or systemic features suggestive of septic arthritis).
- General plan:
  - Send blood test forms to patient’s home.
  - Encourage patient to monitor for any escalation of symptoms.
  - Arrange follow-up appointment after bloodwork completed.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vitals not documented.
  - Comprehensive systems review limited.
  - No mention of smoking/alcohol/substance use status.
  - Detailed medication reconciliation not possible; patient denies regular meds.
  - Further clarification of skin findings and joint examination (swelling extent, fluctuation, erythema) limited by telemedicine.
● Internal conflicts:
  - None identified.
● Transcript quality:
  - Good overall; minor background noise and incomplete sentences, but clinically relevant details accessible. No major omissions.
